flags.detail: test_verdict_banked reads the arc's own STEP3_VERDICT.md and asserts it contains the arc's own claimed verdict string — this cannot fail unless someone edits the file, and does not independently establish the kill result.

The numeric coincidence k+2=5 matching the discriminant 5 elsewhere in the project is exactly the bit-vs-value type-match the seat's rules flag; the arc correctly refuses to accept it as a derivation and marks the level k=3 as inserted, not selected.
'Without a derivation, it is not a falsifiable prediction of the core' — lambda/h=1 is used as input, motivated not derived, matching the pattern flagged throughout the B17-B47 campaign.

The 'convention' that fixed roots belong to the theta+1 (symmetric) sector is explicitly stated in probe.py's own docstring as 'fixed empirically by SL(3)' -- i.e. calibrated to reproduce one known answer, then applied to predict SL(5). The arc itself is honest about this ('not proved... only the height-2 sign/direct split') but it is a genuine risk that the labeling convention was reverse-engineered from the one case it needed to match.

the "literal shared involution" claim rests on both W_N charge-conjugation and Dickson m-parity being instances of the SAME abstract A_{n-1} involution (-w0) acting on a degree-k invariant — a genuine algebraic identity, not a coincidence of dimension, but the FINDINGS text itself explicitly warns the dynamical extension (metallic eigenvalues = higher-spin CFT spectrum) is SPECULATIVE-ANALOGY with no supporting computation, i.e. the arc correctly self-flags where the type-match stops being evidence.

the F2 result rests on both the cusp value and the quantum-group [2]_q value being the same cyclotomic number 2cos(pi/k) — the arc itself calls the deeper reading ("anyonic TQFT") a claim resting "on nothing more than 'both are roots of unity'" and correctly labels it SPECULATIVE-ANALOGY rather than a genuine physics bridge.
